digest.component_or_area: workflow step registry and seam tests
propositions: Headroom guards on plan_review/workflow_ops.py and llm/config.py are missing, leaving files with high regrowth risk (794 and 793 LOC respectively) unprotected
Step registration depends on import side effects via @register_step decorator writing to process-global STEP_REGISTRY, with no static assertion that registration imports survive refactoring
An unregistered workflow step cannot be caught by schema validation, linter, or existing test_contracts.py — only by runtime WorkflowError on an executed path, leaving a latent hazard
The gate_dispatch_seam.py assertion message claims finalize_verdict call sites exist in gate_dispatch.py, but all five sites were moved to plan_review_recovery.py and plan_review/workflow_ops.py

In-process assertions on STEP_REGISTRY are masked by prior test imports that populate the process-global registry, making any guard that does not use subprocess isolation unable to detect missing imports
No mechanism asserts that every uses: value in gates/plan-review.yaml resolves to a registered step independent of test execution order or prior imports
